insights.quote: We believe that we are not smarter than the market. So, when a group of stocks is outperforming, we believe that the market is telling us something. So, for example, if technology stocks and more quality stocks outperform, we will have more of those stocks and we will still declare of, for example, value stock. And in contrary, if we have a period where value shines and the large cap tech names doesn't perform, we will adapt and have more of those names.
insights.summary: Momentum strategy respects market signals rather than trying to outsmart the market, adapting portfolio composition based on which stocks/sectors are currently outperforming.
insights.speaker: Ivar Harstveit

insights.quote: Our ideal buy is a company that has a long-term trend, maybe 12 months, and then some short-term weakness. And that is hopefully just some short-term noise. So for example, a company that has trended upwards, and there has been some sentiment in the market, and the company has performed slightly weaker during the last month, and it's probably just noise. And if we also see that the company has strong fundamental trend, like the estimate revisions and everything positive in the company is still there, we can begin to build a position. And also the advantage of doing it that way is that if we are wrong, we can cut the loss earlier.
insights.summary: The optimal entry point is after a long-term uptrend followed by short-term weakness, combining price trends with fundamental confirmation while maintaining ability to exit quickly if wrong.

summary: This episode discusses momentum management strategy with Ivar Harstveit from Delphi Global, explaining how they combine price trend analysis with fundamental analysis to identify stocks in positive trends. The strategy emphasizes flexibility, adapting to market conditions rather than predicting them, and maintaining a portfolio of 40-50 stocks based on both technical and fundamental trends.
key_takeaways: Momentum strategy combines price trends with fundamental analysis
Portfolio of 40-50 stocks with emphasis on trend stability and estimate revisions
Strategy adapts to market conditions across growth, value, and quality stocks
Uses long-term trends (6-12 months) with preference for buying on short-term weakness
Can serve as a diversification tool alongside traditional index funds
